claim: Liu et al. trained their hexapod PPO+AMP controller using 4096 parallel robots for 50,000 episodes with 1000 steps per episode on a single RTX 3090Ti, taking approximately 35 hours.
stance_target: hexapod PPO+AMP training requires ~35 hours on a single high-end GPU
scope_conditions: IsaacGym simulator, PhantomX-class hexapod, single RTX 3090Ti, PPO+AMP, flat+complex terrain curriculum
quoted_support: We created the terrains in the IsaacGym and trained 4096 robots simultaneously. Each episode involved 1000 steps over 20 seconds, with early termination if the condition was met. The policy ran at a control frequency of 50 Hz. We conducted 50,000 episodes, and the training took about 35 hours on a NVIDIA RTX 3090Ti GPU.

claim: The implied total environment steps for the Liu et al. hexapod run is 4096 x 1000 x 50,000 = 204.8 billion, but this is a ceiling; early termination means effective steps are lower.
stance_target: total step count for hexapod PPO+AMP run
scope_conditions: Derived from reported numbers; paper does not state total steps explicitly
quoted_support: Each episode involved 1000 steps over 20 seconds, with early termination if the condition was met. We conducted 50,000 episodes.

claim: AMP motion priors for the hexapod were generated by trajectory optimization (TO) on flat terrain, producing 8.6 seconds of tripod gait data covering forward, backward, lateral, steering, and combined motions.
stance_target: TO-generated scaffold data can serve as AMP prior for hexapod locomotion
scope_conditions: PhantomX-class hexapod, flat terrain, TO-generated dataset
quoted_support: The resulting trajectories last 8.6 seconds and cover forward, backward, lateral, steering, and combined motions, each maintaining a consistent gait cycle.

claim: The asymmetric Actor-Critic with AMP style reward achieved velocity perturbation tolerance of +/-0.803 m/s, outperforming RMA (+/-0.738), Concurrent (+/-0.463), Baseline (+/-0.201), and MPC (+/-0.112).
stance_target: AMP-guided training produces more robust hexapod controllers than pure PPO or MPC
scope_conditions: Flat terrain, Y-axis velocity perturbations, 5 random seeds, same low-level network across baselines

claim: The Liu et al. hexapod training is a single undivided PPO+AMP run with no separate BC pretrain or DR finetune stage reported.
stance_target: training stage decomposition in hexapod PPO+AMP
scope_conditions: Paper describes one training phase; DR parameters are randomized throughout training, not as a separate finetune
quoted_support: We randomize dynamic parameters for both robots and environments to reflect differences between real and simulated conditions.

claim: The hexapod discriminator network has two hidden layers [1024, 512] taking concatenated (s_t, s_{t+1}) AMP state transitions as input; the actor uses [256, 128, 64] MLP.
stance_target: network architecture for AMP discriminator in hexapod locomotion

claim: The Liu et al. hexapod paper trains on complex terrains (stairs 3-20 cm, slopes 5-30 degrees) and demonstrates successful outdoor transfer on 46m of uneven grassland at 0.5 m/s without visual input.
stance_target: AMP-guided sim-to-real transfer enables blind locomotion on challenging terrain
scope_conditions: Real PhantomX-class hexapod, proprioception only, no camera
quoted_support: we navigated the robot at 0.5 m/s across a flower bed with a 15 cm step and over approximately 46 m of uneven grassland
